zh.summary: 分開判讀七組協定的服務回應、身分驗證與實際權限，讓列舉結論符合證據。

sourceBody.text: 這一課看起來要學 NTP、IPsec、VoIP、IPv6、BGP、Telnet、TFTP 七種技術，好像很複雜。但其實有一個共同的觀念：
你能從網路服務取得資訊，不代表你能登入它；能登入，也不代表你有權限控制它。
這就是 CEH M04「Enumeration（列舉）」最重要的觀念。接下來把這七種技術放進同一個故事，理解它們在網路工程中的角色，以及資安人員應該如何判斷證據。
本課延續 M04-09 的協定與證據判讀，補充初學者需要的網路基礎。
一、先把網路想成一棟辦公大樓
假設你管理一棟擁有 500 位員工的大樓，裡面有電腦、電話、門禁、網路設備與伺服器。

visual.caption: 六組大樓角色，七種協定用途
visual.description: 各組平行比較；Telnet 與 TFTP 是兩種不同服務，卡片之間沒有流程箭頭。

items.title: NTP｜標準時鐘
items.body: 讓全部設備的時間一致

items.title: IPsec／IKE｜安全通道
items.body: 保護遠端連線與傳輸

items.title: VoIP／SIP｜電話總機
items.body: 協助撥號、接聽與傳送語音

items.title: IPv6｜地址與鄰居
items.body: 識別設備與發現路由器

items.title: BGP｜跨網路導航
items.body: 讓不同大型網路交換路線

items.title: Telnet／TFTP｜舊式管理室
items.body: 遠端終端機與簡易檔案傳輸

sourceBody.text: 它們的功能不同，所以我們不能用同一套判斷方法，把所有回應都認定為安全漏洞。
二、CEH 列舉到底在做什麼？
把 CEH 的 M03、M04、M05 串起來：

visual.caption: M03 → M04 → M05：從入口到風險
visual.description: 箭頭表示課程的判讀順序；發現服務後仍需證據，才能支持弱點結論。

items.title: M03｜Scanning：找到大樓入口
items.body: 有哪些主機與服務？

items.title: M04｜Enumeration：詢問櫃檯資訊
items.body: 服務願意提供什麼？

items.title: M05｜Vulnerability：分析保護弱點
items.body: 是否存在可證實的風險？

sourceBody.text: 你掃描到某個 Port 開啟，只能說那裡可能有服務；你取得服務資訊，也不能立刻說它有漏洞。
教材提供了五個證據層次：

visual.caption: 網路服務的證據判讀階梯
visual.description: 由上到下比較證據強度；箭頭不是通用登入流程，也不表示權限會自動增加。

items.title: 1. 發現服務
items.body: 找到一個可能提供服務的入口。

items.title: 2. 取得回應
items.body: 對方真的回應你的請求。

items.title: 3. 取得資訊
items.body: 對方揭露部分版本、設定或狀態。

items.title: 4. 驗證身分
items.body: 對方確認你是誰（部分服務不需要這個步驟）。

items.title: 5. 驗證操作權限
items.body: 確認你真正能讀取、修改或執行什麼。

sourceBody.text: 這是證據強度的分析框架，不是所有協定都必須走過的固定流程。
三、NTP：為什麼時間一致關係到資安？
NTP（Network Time Protocol）
想像警察在調查一個案件，三支監視器的時間各差了幾分鐘。
即使三支監視器都錄到了影像，你仍然可能把事件發生順序弄錯。
電腦也一樣。假設有三台設備記錄同一個入侵事件：
如果沒有時間同步，資安調查很可能出現錯誤結論。
NTP 使用常見的 UDP 123 連接埠，讓設備向時間來源同步。
Stratum 又是什麼？
它代表時間同步來源的階層。

visual.caption: NTP：時間同步從哪一層傳下來？
visual.description: 向下箭頭表示本例的時間來源關係；Stratum 0 是參考時鐘，不是一般 NTP 伺服器。

items.title: Stratum 0
items.body: 原子鐘、GNSS 等參考時鐘

items.title: Stratum 1
items.body: 直接連接參考時鐘的 NTP 伺服器

items.title: Stratum 2
items.body: 向上一層伺服器同步

items.title: Stratum 3、4…
items.body: 從各自的上游時間來源繼續同步

visual.caption: NTP 多層同步：同層設備彼此平行
visual.description: 框線分組表示 Stratum 1–4；向下箭頭表示候選時間來源傳遞，同層 ↔ 表示可配置的對等關係。上游可多選，實際同步來源由選擇程序決定；圖中不保證準確性、完整備援或管理權限。

items.body: 原子鐘／GNSS 參考時鐘

sourceBody.text: 多層圖保留同層對等、多個上游與共用鏈路：同層設備是平行角色。各節點列出來源與對等端點，實際來源仍由 NTP 選擇程序決定；連線示意不保證準確性或管理權限。
要注意：Stratum 數字較小，不等於一定比較準確。同步狀態、來源品質與網路延遲也很重要。
從 CEH 的角度，假設 NTP 回答你現在是 10:00，這代表時間服務正常回應；不代表你能讀取它的管理設定，更不代表可以修改時間伺服器。
[RFC 5905](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5905.html)
四、IPsec／IKE：VPN 為什麼不是連上就能進去？
想像你在家工作，希望連到公司的內部系統。
VPN 可以提供安全的網路通道，其中 IPsec 是常見的保護技術，而 IKE（Internet Key Exchange）負責協商保護方式與驗證身分。

visual.caption: 家裡電腦 → VPN 閘道 → 公司內網
visual.description: 這條路徑是角色示意。下列三項依序說明初始協商、身分驗證及可用性檢查；它們不是 IKEv1 的階段，也不是三個固定 IKEv2 交換。

items.title: IKE_SA_INIT：談好保護方式
items.body: 例如雙方協商加密演算法、交換建立金鑰所需的材料。

items.title: IKE_AUTH：驗證雙方身分
items.body: 使用憑證或其他配置的驗證方式，確認連線對象；通常也協商第一組 CHILD_SA。

items.title: 確認可用的資料通道
items.body: 還要有適當的 IPsec 資料安全關聯與路由、存取政策，才可能真正使用內部資源。

sourceBody.text: 假設你收到 `IKE_SA_INIT` 的回覆。
你可以說 VPN 服務回應了初始協商，但不能說自己已經登入 VPN。因為還沒有確認身分驗證成功，更沒有確認內部資源的存取權限。
還有一個很容易考錯的地方：
IP Protocol 50 不是 Port 50。 Port 是 TCP/UDP 等傳輸協定使用的編號；IP Protocol Number 是 IP 封包表明承載哪一種上層協定的編號。
[RFC 7296](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7296.html) · [RFC 4301](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4301.html)
五、VoIP：為什麼電話已加密，聲音卻可能被聽到？
這個觀念非常重要，尤其是電話服務、客服中心或電話錄音系統。
VoIP 是透過 IP 網路傳送電話服務。裡面有兩件不同的工作：

visual.caption: SIP 與 RTP：兩條不同的工作線
visual.description: 每列的 ↔ 表示通話端之間該類資料的雙向交換，不表示 SIP 訊令與 RTP 語音必走相同路徑；兩列彼此平行。

items.title: SIP：通話控制 ↔
items.body:
撥打方 ↔ 撥號、響鈴、接通 ↔ 接聽方

TLS 可保護 SIP 訊令的特定傳輸區段。

items.title: RTP：傳輸媒體 ↔
items.body:
聲音輸入 ↔ 語音封包 ↔ 聲音輸出

媒體需要另外確認 SRTP 等保護及金鑰協商。

sourceBody.text: 簡單來說：
SIP 像電話總機，RTP 像真正講話的聲音。
假設 SIP 已經使用 TLS 加密，但是語音媒體仍使用沒有加密的一般 RTP，那麼在能觀察媒體封包的網路位置，聲音仍有被還原的風險。
所以做 CEH 查核時，不能因為看到 TCP 5061（常見 SIP over TLS）就宣布「整套電話系統已加密」。
應分開確認 SIP 訊令、RTP/SRTP 媒體、金鑰交換及存取控制。
[RFC 3261](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3261.html) · [RFC 3550](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3550.html) · [RFC 3711](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3711.html)
六、IPv6：為什麼電腦看到的鄰居不代表全部設備？
IPv6 使用 128-bit 位址，例如：
其中 `fe80::/10` 是 Link-Local 位址範圍，主要用於本地鏈路通訊。
IPv6 有一套稱為 Neighbor Discovery（ND）的機制，可把它想成大樓內尋找鄰居及詢問路由器的方式。

rows: 請問某個 IPv6 位址的鄰居在哪裡？
我來回覆或公告鄰居資訊
請問附近有哪些路由器？
路由器提供網路設定資訊

sourceBody.text: 它們使用 ICMPv6，而不是 TCP/UDP Port。
假設你的電腦在鄰居表中只看到兩筆紀錄。這只代表目前有兩筆快取，並不表示整個區域只有兩台設備。
有些設備可能尚未與你通訊、快取已經過期，或者同一台設備有多個 IPv6 位址。
在 Ubuntu 上，可以安全查看自己電腦的鄰居快取：
ip -6 neigh show
這個指令主要是在讀本機核心保留的資訊，不是在掃描整個網路。可在有 iproute2 的 Ubuntu 終端機執行；每列通常包含鄰居位址、介面及狀態，沒有紀錄時也可能不輸出任何列。這裡未提供真實設備的執行結果。
另外，不要認為封鎖全部 ICMPv6 就更安全。IPv6 的鄰居探索、路徑 MTU 探索等機制依賴特定 ICMPv6 訊息，全部封鎖反而可能導致連線故障。
[RFC 4291](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4291.html) · [RFC 4861](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4861.html) · [RFC 4890](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4890.html)
七、BGP：網際網路為什麼知道資料該往哪裡走？
想像你要從台灣寄包裹到美國。
台灣物流公司不必知道美國每條街道，但要知道接下來應把包裹交給哪一家物流網路。
BGP（Border Gateway Protocol）就像各大型網路之間交換運送路線的機制。
這裡會碰到兩個詞：
AS（Autonomous System，自治系統） 是由共同路由政策管理的一組 IP 網路；ASN 則是該自治系統的編號。
例如教材中的假想路徑：
代表某份路由資訊中的 AS 路徑，但不等於封包一定經過你想像中的那些實體路由器。
BGP 常見 TCP 179。透過公開的 Looking Glass，你可能查到某個觀測點看到的 BGP 路由。
然而，你看到路由資料，不代表你有權更改路由。這就是「資訊可見」和「管理授權」的差別。

visual.caption: BGP 公告與 AS_PATH：回到自己便辨識迴圈
visual.description: 四個 AS 形成菱形。箭頭表示此例公告方向：AS64500 → AS64497 → AS64496 → AS64498 → AS64500；回到來源的公告含本身 ASN，因此排除。這不是資料封包的轉送箭頭。

sourceBody.text: 圖中前綴用文件示例 192.0.2.0/24，四個 AS 也改用文件示例編號。公告每經一個外部 AS，該 AS 會把自己的編號加到 AS_PATH 前端；本例依序出現 64500、64497 64500、64496 64497 64500、64498 64496 64497 64500。當公告回到 AS64500，接收端發現路徑已含自己，便排除這條迴圈路由。箭頭表示路由公告方向；一般資料封包朝目的前綴的轉送方向與這個公告方向不同。這是簡化示意，不是實測路由或全部選路規則。
在資安上，BGP 還涉及 Route Hijacking（路由劫持）、錯誤路由宣告、前綴過濾與 RPKI。RPKI 可以協助驗證某來源 AS 是否被授權宣告特定 IP 前綴，但不能單靠它保證整條 AS_PATH 都正確。
[RFC 4271](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4271.html) · [RFC 5398](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5398.html) · [RFC 6811](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6811.html)
八、Telnet、TFTP：為什麼老技術容易產生安全疑慮？
Telnet｜遠端文字終端機
想像在自己的電腦上操作另一台電腦的命令列。傳統 Telnet 常見 TCP 23，沒有提供現代所需的傳輸加密，帳號、密碼及指令可能被沿途具有封包觀察能力的人看見。
現代遠端管理通常優先使用 SSH。
TFTP｜簡易檔案傳輸
想像設備知道某份設定檔的檔名，就向伺服器要求傳送。TFTP 常見使用 UDP 69 接收初始請求，之後使用另外選定的 UDP 埠傳輸資料。
基本 TFTP 沒有標準的使用者登入機制，也沒有一般的目錄瀏覽功能。
重點在於：TFTP 沒有登入畫面，不代表所有檔案都可以讀寫。伺服器仍可藉由來源、路徑和檔案權限限制存取。
同樣地，看到 Telnet 登入畫面，也不代表已經取得遠端終端機權限。

visual.caption: Telnet：登入提示與登入後畫面分開判讀
visual.description: 參考圖含 guest 登入與歡迎文字；此處用合成終端紀錄分開兩種狀態，沒有連線到圖中的網站。兩欄比較，不代表登入一定成功。

items.title: 僅看到登入提示
items.body:
login:

這只能證明登入入口回應，尚無帳號通過驗證的證據。

items.title: 合成登入後示意
items.body:
login: guest
Welcome to the training terminal.

歡迎文字是另一個觀察層次；可用指令與資源仍受帳號權限限制。

visual.caption: TFTP：要求檔案、回應與存取限制
visual.description: 左右表示用戶端與伺服器；↔ 表示請求／資料及確認的往返，不保證任意檔案都可讀寫。示意不包含真實傳輸。

items.title: 用戶端｜依已知檔名提出要求
items.body:
要求讀取 training.cfg → 伺服器 UDP 69

後續以雙方選定的 UDP TID 交換資料與確認。

items.title: 伺服器｜依政策回應
items.body:
← 允許時傳回特定檔案，拒絕時回覆錯誤或不提供資料。

來源、路徑與檔案權限決定可用範圍；基本協定沒有目錄瀏覽或使用者登入。

sourceBody.text: [RFC 854](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc854.html) · [RFC 1350](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1350.html) · [RFC 4251](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4251.html)
九、七種協定的 CEH 重點總整理

rows: 時間回應不等於管理權限
協商回應不等於 VPN 登入
訊令加密不等於語音加密
鄰居快取不是完整資產清單
看到路由不等於可修改路由
登入提示不等於登入成功
檔案服務存在不等於可任意讀寫

sourceBody.text: SIP 常見 UDP／TCP 5060；TLS over TCP 常見 5061。這些是常見值，不是不可改變的規則；發現某個 Port，仍要確認實際提供的服務。
十、真正做 CEH 查核時，如何寫出專業的判斷？
假設你在經過授權的測試環境中，發現一台 VPN 伺服器會回應 `IKE_SA_INIT`。
不好的報告會寫：
已發現 VPN 弱點，攻擊者可能進入內網。
因為這份結論沒有足夠證據。
比較專業的紀錄方式如下：

visual.caption: VPN 查核紀錄：從實際觀察到下一步驗證
visual.description: 三列是同一份合成報告的欄位；沒有真實 VPN 測試，也沒有已找到漏洞的結論。

items.title: 實際觀察
items.body: 測試端點對 IKEv2 初始協商提供有效回應。

items.title: 證據界線
items.body: 可證明服務回應，但尚無身分驗證成功或內網資源存取的證據。

items.title: 下一步驗證
items.body: 在授權範圍內，使用核准的測試帳號確認 VPN 驗證、通道建立及存取控制是否符合政策。

sourceBody.text: 這樣才能分清楚四件事：正常服務、資訊揭露、錯誤設定，以及真正具有安全影響的弱點。
十一、理解檢核：你能不能像 CEH 分析人員一樣判斷？
1. 某台 VPN 伺服器回覆 IKE_SA_INIT，你會如何判斷？
A. 已成功登入 VPN
B. 只確認初始協商有回應
C. 已取得公司內網權限

paragraphs: 答案 B。IKE_SA_INIT 回應只確認初始協商有回覆。A 還缺成功驗證身分的證據；C 也缺實際內網資源存取與授權證據。

sourceBody.text: 2. SIP 已使用 TLS，是否足以證明通話聲音已加密？
A. 是，所有語音都會加密
B. 否，還需要驗證媒體傳輸的保護
C. 是，只要使用 5061 即可

paragraphs: 答案 B。SIP 訊令與語音媒體是兩條不同的工作線。A 將訊令 TLS 擴大成所有語音加密；C 只憑 5061 埠號也無法證明實際媒體保護。須另外確認 SRTP 等保護及金鑰協商。

sourceBody.text: 3. 你的 IPv6 鄰居表只有兩筆資料，代表什麼？
A. 整個網路只有兩台設備
B. 其他設備一定被隱藏
C. 本機目前有兩筆鄰居快取

paragraphs: 答案 C。本機目前有兩筆鄰居快取。A 無法代表完整設備數量；B 也不能從缺少快取推論其他設備被隱藏。尚未通訊、快取過期與同機多位址都影響紀錄。

sourceBody.text: 4. 某 TFTP 伺服器可以回應請求，是否代表任何檔案都能下載？
A. 是，因為 TFTP 沒有登入機制
B. 否，還受到伺服器設定及檔案權限限制
C. 是，而且可以任意修改檔案

paragraphs: 答案 B。伺服器設定及檔案權限仍限制可讀取的範圍。A 把沒有登入機制當成無限制讀取；C 更把回應擴大成任意修改。基本 TFTP 也沒有目錄瀏覽功能。

sourceBody.text: 先作答，再展開各題的參考答案與解析；本頁不儲存答案或計算學習進度。
這一課最值得建立的能力，不是死背七個協定的 Port，而是面對任何新的網路服務，都能回答三個問題：我實際看到了什麼？這能證明什麼？還需要哪些證據才能做出安全結論？
掌握這三個問題，後續學 CEH M05 弱點分析、滲透測試及資安稽核時，才能避免把服務的正常功能誤認為漏洞。

en.summary: Distinguish service responses, authentication and actual permissions across seven protocol groups, so enumeration conclusions fit the evidence.

sourceBody.text: This lesson introduces NTP, IPsec, VoIP, IPv6, BGP, Telnet and TFTP. Although their roles differ, one idea connects them:
Obtaining information from a network service does not establish that you can sign in; signing in does not establish that you are authorized to control it.
That distinction is central to CEH M04, Enumeration. Place these technologies in one story to understand their network roles and how a security analyst should interpret evidence.
This lesson continues M04-09’s protocol and evidence analysis with the network foundations a beginner needs.
1. Imagine a network as an office building
Suppose you manage a building with 500 employees. It contains computers, telephones, access controls, network equipment and servers.

visual.caption: Six building roles, seven protocol groups
visual.description: These are parallel comparisons. Telnet and TFTP are distinct services; no arrows imply a sequence between cards.

items.title: NTP | Standard clock
items.body: Keep device clocks consistent.

items.title: IPsec / IKE | Secure channel
items.body: Protect remote connections and traffic.

items.title: VoIP / SIP | Telephone switchboard
items.body: Support dialing, answering and voice transport.

items.title: IPv6 | Addresses and neighbors
items.body: Identify devices and discover routers.

items.title: BGP | Inter-network navigation
items.body: Exchange routes between large networks.

items.title: Telnet / TFTP | Older management room
items.body: Remote terminals and simple file transfer.

sourceBody.text: These services do different jobs. A single interpretation rule cannot turn every response into a security vulnerability.
2. What does CEH enumeration actually do?
Connect CEH M03, M04 and M05:

visual.caption: M03 → M04 → M05: from entry points to risk
visual.description: Arrows show the curriculum’s reasoning sequence. Discovering a service still requires evidence before a vulnerability conclusion.

items.title: M03 | Scanning: find building entrances
items.body: Which hosts and services exist?

items.title: M04 | Enumeration: ask the reception desk
items.body: What will the service reveal?

items.title: M05 | Vulnerability: analyze protection weaknesses
items.body: Is there a risk supported by evidence?

sourceBody.text: Finding an open port only suggests a service may be present. Obtaining information from that service still does not establish a vulnerability.
The lesson distinguishes five evidence levels:

visual.caption: Five levels of service evidence
visual.description: Read downward as a comparison of evidence strength; arrows are neither a universal login process nor automatic privilege gains.

items.title: 1. Discover a service
items.body: Find a possible service entry point.

items.title: 2. Receive a response
items.body: The service actually answers your request.

items.title: 3. Obtain information
items.body: The service reveals some version, configuration or state information.

items.title: 4. Authenticate
items.body: The service confirms who you are; some services do not require this step.

items.title: 5. Verify operating permissions
items.body: Confirm what you can actually read, change or execute.

sourceBody.text: This is a framework for analyzing evidence strength, not a mandatory sequence that every protocol follows.
3. NTP: why does consistent time matter to security?
NTP stands for Network Time Protocol.
Imagine investigators reviewing three surveillance cameras whose clocks differ by several minutes.
All three may record the event, yet investigators can still reconstruct its sequence incorrectly.
Computers have the same problem. Suppose three devices record the same intrusion:
Without time synchronization, a security investigation can reach the wrong conclusion.
NTP commonly uses UDP 123 to synchronize devices with a time source.
What is stratum?
Stratum describes the hierarchy of time synchronization sources.

visual.caption: NTP: where does the time come from?
visual.description: Downward arrows show the source of time in this example; Stratum 0 is a reference clock, not an ordinary NTP server.

items.title: Stratum 0
items.body: Reference clocks such as atomic clocks or GNSS

items.title: Stratum 1
items.body: NTP servers directly connected to a reference clock

items.title: Stratum 2
items.body: Synchronizes to a server one level above

items.title: Stratum 3, 4…
items.body: Continue synchronizing from their respective upstream time sources.

visual.caption: NTP hierarchy: peers share a level
visual.description: Boundaries group Stratum 1–4. Downward arrows show candidate time-source relationships; same-level ↔ indicates configurable peering. Multiple upstream candidates are possible; selection determines the actual source. The diagram guarantees neither accuracy, complete redundancy nor management access.

items.title: Stratum 0
items.body: Atomic / GNSS reference clock

items.title: S1-A
items.body: Reference clock; peer S1-B

items.title: S1-B
items.body: Reference clock; peer S1-A

items.title: S2-A
items.body: Upstream S1-A; peer S2-B

items.title: S2-B
items.body: Upstream S1-B; peer S2-A

items.title: S3-A
items.body: Candidates S2-A / S2-B; peer S3-B

items.title: S3-B
items.body: Candidates S2-A / S2-B; peer S3-A / S3-C

items.title: S3-C
items.body: Candidates S2-A / S2-B; peer S3-D / S3-B

items.title: S3-D
items.body: Candidates S2-A / S2-B; peer S3-C

items.title: S4-A
items.body: Shared-link sources S3-A / S3-B

items.title: S4-B
items.body: Shared-link sources S3-A / S3-B

items.title: S4-C
items.body: Shared-link sources S3-A / S3-B

items.title: S4-D
items.body: Shared-link sources S3-C / S3-D

items.title: S4-E
items.body: Shared-link sources S3-C / S3-D

sourceBody.text: The hierarchy preserves same-level peering, multiple upstream sources and shared links. Devices at the same level are parallel roles. Each node names its source and peer endpoints; NTP’s selection procedure determines the actual source. The illustrated relationships guarantee neither accuracy nor management access.
A smaller stratum number does not necessarily mean greater accuracy. Synchronization state, source quality and network delay also matter.
For CEH analysis, an NTP reply saying that it is 10:00 establishes a responsive time service. It does not establish permission to read management settings or change the time server.
[RFC 5905](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5905.html)
4. IPsec / IKE: why is a VPN response not a successful connection?
Imagine working at home and needing access to internal company systems.
A VPN can provide a protected network channel. IPsec is a common protection technology; IKE, Internet Key Exchange, negotiates protection and authenticates identities.

visual.caption: Home computer → VPN gateway → internal network
visual.description: The path identifies roles. The three items explain initial negotiation, authentication and usability checks; they are neither IKEv1 phases nor three mandatory IKEv2 exchanges.

items.title: IKE_SA_INIT: negotiate protection
items.body: Negotiate algorithms and exchange material needed to establish keys.

items.title: IKE_AUTH: authenticate both parties
items.body: Confirm identity using certificates or another configured method; normally negotiate the first CHILD_SA too.

items.title: Verify a usable data channel
items.body: Suitable IPsec data SAs, routing and access policies are also needed to use internal resources.

sourceBody.text: Suppose you receive an `IKE_SA_INIT` response.

You may report that the VPN service answered initial negotiation. You cannot report a successful VPN sign-in: authentication has not yet been established, and neither has permission to access internal resources.
Another common source of confusion is the meaning of these numbers:
IP Protocol 50 is not Port 50. Ports are identifiers used by transports such as TCP and UDP; the IP Protocol Number identifies the protocol carried by an IP packet.
[RFC 7296](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7296.html) · [RFC 4301](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4301.html)
5. VoIP: why might audio remain exposed when telephone signaling is encrypted?
This distinction matters for telephone services, contact centers and call-recording systems.
VoIP carries telephone services over an IP network. It involves two distinct jobs:

visual.caption: SIP and RTP: two distinct flows
visual.description: Each ↔ denotes bidirectional exchange of that data type between call parties. Signaling and media need not follow the same route; the two rows are parallel.

items.title: SIP: call control ↔
items.body:
Calling party ↔ dialing, ringing, connection ↔ receiving party

TLS can protect a particular SIP signaling transport segment.

items.title: RTP: media transport ↔
items.body:
Audio input ↔ voice packets ↔ audio output

Check media protection such as SRTP and key negotiation separately.

sourceBody.text: Put simply:
SIP is like the telephone switchboard; RTP carries the actual spoken audio.
Suppose SIP uses TLS, but the audio media uses ordinary unencrypted RTP. At a network position that can observe the media packets, reconstructing the audio may still be possible.
During a CEH review, observing TCP 5061, commonly SIP over TLS, therefore does not establish that the entire telephone system is encrypted.
Check SIP signaling, RTP/SRTP media, key exchange and access controls separately.
[RFC 3261](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3261.html) · [RFC 3550](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3550.html) · [RFC 3711](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3711.html)
6. IPv6: why do visible neighbors not represent every device?
IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses, for example:
`fe80::/10` is the Link-Local address range, primarily used for communication on the local link.
IPv6’s Neighbor Discovery, or ND, provides mechanisms comparable to finding neighbors and asking routers for information inside a building.

rows: Where is the neighbor at a particular IPv6 address?
Reply with or announce neighbor information.
A router provides network configuration information.

sourceBody.text: These messages use ICMPv6, not TCP or UDP ports.
Suppose your computer’s neighbor table has only two entries. That establishes two current cache records, not that the entire area contains only two devices.
Other devices may not have communicated with you, records may have expired, and one device can have multiple IPv6 addresses.
On Ubuntu, inspect your own computer’s neighbor cache with:
ip -6 neigh show

This command primarily reads information retained by the local kernel; it does not scan the entire network. Run it in an Ubuntu terminal with iproute2 installed. Each row normally includes a neighbor address, interface and state; an empty cache may produce no rows. No real-device execution result is supplied here.
Blocking all ICMPv6 does not automatically improve security. IPv6 neighbor discovery and Path MTU Discovery depend on particular ICMPv6 messages; blocking all of them can break connectivity.
[RFC 4291](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4291.html) · [RFC 4861](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4861.html) · [RFC 4890](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4890.html)
7. BGP: how does the Internet know where to send data?
Imagine sending a parcel from Taiwan to the United States.
The Taiwanese logistics company need not know every American street. It needs to know which logistics network should receive the parcel next.
BGP, Border Gateway Protocol, similarly exchanges routes between large networks.
Two terms are useful:
An AS, Autonomous System, is a group of IP networks managed under a common routing policy. An ASN is its identifying number.
For example, the lesson uses this hypothetical path:
It represents an AS path recorded in route information, not necessarily the physical routers that a packet will traverse.
BGP commonly uses TCP 179. A public Looking Glass may show the routes visible from a particular observation point.
Seeing that information does not authorize changing routes. Information visibility and administrative permission are distinct.

visual.caption: BGP advertisements and AS_PATH: detect a returning loop
visual.description: Four ASes form a diamond. Arrows show this example’s advertisement direction: AS64500 → AS64497 → AS64496 → AS64498 → AS64500. The returning path contains the receiving AS’s own ASN and is excluded. These are not packet-forwarding arrows.

items.title: AS64500 | Origin and loop check
items.body:
Advertise 192.0.2.0/24 → AS64497

Outgoing AS_PATH: 64500

Receive 64498 64496 64497 64500 from AS64498; exclude the loop because it contains own ASN 64500.

items.title: AS64497 | Advertise rightward
items.body:
Receive 64500 from AS64500

Advertise to AS64496: 64497 64500

items.title: AS64496 | Advertise downward
items.body:
Receive 64497 64500 from AS64497

Advertise to AS64498: 64496 64497 64500

sourceBody.text: The diagram uses documentation prefix 192.0.2.0/24 and documentation ASNs for all four ASes. Each external AS prepends its own number when advertising the route onward. This example successively produces 64500, 64497 64500, 64496 64497 64500, and 64498 64496 64497 64500. When the advertisement returns to AS64500, the receiver finds its own ASN already in the path and excludes the looping route. Arrows indicate route advertisements; ordinary packet forwarding toward the destination prefix differs from that advertisement direction. This is a simplified example, not measured routing or a complete account of route selection.

BGP security also involves route hijacking, incorrect route announcements, prefix filtering and RPKI. RPKI can help validate whether an origin AS is authorized to announce a particular prefix; it cannot by itself establish the correctness of the entire AS_PATH.
[RFC 4271](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4271.html) · [RFC 5398](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5398.html) · [RFC 6811](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6811.html)
8. Telnet and TFTP: why do older technologies raise security concerns?
Telnet | Remote text terminal

Imagine operating another computer’s command line from your own computer. Traditional Telnet commonly uses TCP 23 and lacks the transport encryption expected today. Someone able to observe packets along the path may see usernames, passwords and commands.
Modern remote administration normally favors SSH.
TFTP | Simple file transfer
Imagine a device that knows a configuration filename and requests it from a server. TFTP commonly accepts initial requests on UDP 69, then uses separately selected UDP ports for the transfer.
Basic TFTP has no standard user sign-in mechanism or general directory-browsing facility.
The absence of a login screen does not make every file readable or writable. The server can still restrict access by source, path and file permissions.
Likewise, seeing a Telnet login screen does not establish remote terminal access.

visual.caption: Telnet: distinguish a prompt from a post-login screen
visual.description: The reference includes a guest login and welcome text. Synthetic terminal records distinguish the states here; no connection was made to the pictured site. The columns compare states, not guaranteed login success.

items.title: Login prompt only
items.body:
login:

This establishes a responsive sign-in entry point, with no evidence that an account authenticated.

items.title: Synthetic post-login example
items.body:
login: guest
Welcome to the training terminal.

Welcome text is another observation level; commands and resources remain subject to account permissions.

visual.caption: TFTP: file requests, responses and access limits
visual.description: The sides represent client and server. ↔ denotes requests, data and acknowledgments, not arbitrary file permissions. No real transfer was performed.

items.title: Client | Request a known filename
items.body:
Request training.cfg → server UDP 69

Continue data and acknowledgments using the UDP TIDs selected by both sides.

items.title: Server | Respond under policy
items.body:
← Return the particular file if allowed; otherwise respond with an error or provide no data.

Source, path and file permissions define the accessible scope; the base protocol has no directory browsing or user sign-in.

sourceBody.text: [RFC 854](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc854.html) · [RFC 1350](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1350.html) · [RFC 4251](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4251.html)
9. CEH summary of the seven protocol groups

rows: A time reply does not establish management permission.
A negotiation reply does not establish VPN sign-in.
Encrypted signaling does not establish encrypted audio.
The neighbor cache is not a complete asset inventory.
Seeing routes does not authorize modifying them.
A login prompt does not establish successful login.
A file service does not grant arbitrary read/write access.

sourceBody.text: SIP commonly uses UDP or TCP 5060, and TLS over TCP 5061. These are common values, not immutable rules. Discovering a port still requires identifying the actual service.
10. How do you write a professional CEH review conclusion?
Suppose an authorized test environment contains a VPN server that answers `IKE_SA_INIT`.
An unsupported report might say:
A VPN vulnerability was found; an attacker may enter the internal network.
The conclusion lacks sufficient evidence.
A more precise record would read:

visual.caption: VPN review record: observation through next verification
visual.description: The three rows are fields in one synthetic report. No real VPN was tested and no vulnerability was established.

items.title: Observation
items.body: The test endpoint returns a valid response to IKEv2 initial negotiation.

items.title: Evidence boundary
items.body: This establishes a service response; successful authentication and internal-resource access have not been established.

items.title: Next verification
items.body: Within authorization, use an approved test account to check VPN authentication, tunnel establishment and access controls against policy.

sourceBody.text: This distinguishes normal service behavior, information disclosure, misconfiguration and vulnerabilities with an established security impact.
11. Understanding check: can you interpret evidence like a CEH analyst?
1. A VPN server replies to IKE_SA_INIT. How do you interpret it?
A. VPN sign-in succeeded.
B. Only a response to initial negotiation has been established.
C. Access to the company’s internal network has been obtained.

paragraphs: Answer B. An IKE_SA_INIT reply establishes only a response to initial negotiation. A lacks successful authentication evidence; C also lacks actual authorized internal-resource access evidence.

sourceBody.text: 2. SIP uses TLS. Is that sufficient to establish encrypted call audio?
A. Yes; all audio will be encrypted.
B. No; media transport protection still needs verification.
C. Yes; using 5061 is sufficient.

paragraphs: Answer B. SIP signaling and voice media are separate flows. A expands signaling TLS into encryption of all audio; C infers media protection from port 5061 alone. Check protection such as SRTP and key negotiation separately.

sourceBody.text: 3. Your IPv6 neighbor table has only two entries. What does that mean?
A. The entire network contains only two devices.
B. Other devices must be hidden.
C. The local computer currently has two neighbor-cache records.

paragraphs: Answer C. The local computer currently has two neighbor-cache records. A does not establish the complete device count; B cannot infer hidden devices from missing records. No prior communication, cache expiry and multiple addresses per device all affect the records.

sourceBody.text: 4. A TFTP server responds to requests. Does that mean any file can be downloaded?
A. Yes, because TFTP has no sign-in mechanism.
B. No; server configuration and file permissions still apply.
C. Yes, and any file can also be modified.

paragraphs: Answer B. Server configuration and file permissions still restrict readable files. A treats no sign-in as unrestricted reading; C expands a response into arbitrary modification. Basic TFTP also lacks directory browsing.

sourceBody.text: Answer first, then expand each reference answer and explanation. This page does not store answers or calculate learning progress.
The skill to build is asking three questions about any new service: What did I actually observe? What does it establish? What further evidence supports a security conclusion?
These questions support later work in CEH M05 vulnerability analysis, penetration testing and security audits by helping distinguish normal service behavior from vulnerabilities.
